rv.q: It's a typically intriguing response that reframes afresh the issues running through it
It may be odd, but this Tempest is absolutely in the spirit of Shakespeare’s ‘insubstantial pageant’, as the man himself put it.
But there’s still a certain pathos that comes with leaving this space, knowing it’ll be quite some time before you see a Shakespeare play that hums with so much mischief and life.
The drama feels unsatisfactory when it is entirely sacrificed for the high concept, and possibly bamboozling for someone encountering it for the first time.
Equal parts haunting and frustrating, sinister and unpredictable, this is a challenging treatment of a familiar play.
There are moments of theatrical magic, but though the unevenness may be deliberate, it can be trying.
This staging is imaginative and theatrically rich, and is sure to be a night out that audiences won’t soon forget.
Yet despite the many virtues of making this a conceptual experiment rather than an enchanted isle, at the end it feels all too easy to leave it.
This is a performance where it is a privilege to get lost in the power of theatre.

cn.t: Tim Crouch's radical, metatheatrical reimagining of Shakespeare's classic divides critics. While some praise its intelligent, daring experimentation and fresh approach, others find the high-concept production painfully artificial and leaden.
